title: Wire up or delete the unused SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository

evidence.quote:
/// All key strings and default values are centralised here rather than
/// being scattered across multiple Riverpod notifiers.

why: SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository is constructed nowhere in lib/ outside its own constructor declaration -- a repo-wide grep confirms zero call sites. Its doc comment claims prefs are centralised here instead of being scattered across notifiers, but every one of the 5 preference providers in notification_providers.dart still reads/writes SharedPreferences key-by-key inline via the static key helpers, exactly the scattered pattern the class claims to replace. It has zero test coverage and misleads a reader into believing there is a repository DI seam here when there isn't one.
recommendation: Either finish the migration (route the 5 providers' load/save through a provider constructing this repository) or delete the class and the interface's now-pointless abstract load()/save(), keeping only the static key helpers that are actually used.
acceptance_criteria: Either a provider constructs SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository and the 5 notifiers call load()/save() through it with a test exercising both methods; or the class and abstract methods are removed and dart analyze stays clean.
